title: ML system design interview
description: Prepare for the ML system design round: the open-ended interview where you design a recommender, a search ranker, an ads model, a RAG assistant or an LLM serving platform on a whiteboard. Each track opens with a lesson that teaches the theory with diagrams: the answer framework, back-of-the-envelope numbers, data and feature pipelines, retrieval and ranking funnels, evaluation and experiments, LLM serving (KV cache, batching, latency and cost), and RAG. Short questions drill the numbers and trade-offs interviewers probe; Python exercises build the pieces you would sketch (point-in-time joins, ranking metrics, diversity re-ranking, drift checks, rank fusion, a batching simulator and a serving capacity planner), each with an editorial. The last track walks through complete designs and then asks you to write your own. No GPU needed.

sources.title: Designing Machine Learning Systems (Chip Huyen, O'Reilly, 2022)
sources.note: Data, features, training, deployment and monitoring as one system: the backbone of the first five tracks.

sources.title: Rules of Machine Learning (Martin Zinkevich, Google)
sources.note: Practical rules on launching a first model, features, training/serving skew and objectives.

sources.title: AIMLInterviews (Alireza Dirafzoon, MIT)
sources.note: The interview guide whose ML system design notes set this course's topics. Questions, rubrics and code here were written for this course.

sources.title: Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations (Covington, Adams, Sargin, RecSys 2016)
sources.note: The two-stage candidate generation and ranking funnel.

sources.title: Sampling-Bias-Corrected Neural Modeling for Large Corpus Item Recommendations (Yi et al., RecSys 2019)
sources.note: Two-tower retrieval with in-batch negatives and its sampling correction.

sources.title: Practical Lessons from Predicting Clicks on Ads at Facebook (He et al., 2014)
sources.note: Calibration, normalized cross-entropy and data freshness in a production CTR model.

sources.title: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using HNSW graphs (Malkov and Yashunin)
sources.note: The graph index behind most vector search.

sources.title: Michelangelo: Uber's machine learning platform
sources.note: An online and offline feature store and the training/serving split.

sources.title: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments (Kohavi, Tang, Xu)
sources.note: A/B tests, sample sizes, guardrail metrics and sample ratio mismatch.

sources.title: The use of MMR, diversity-based reranking (Carbonell and Goldstein, SIGIR 1998)
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Cormack, Clarke, Buettcher, SIGIR 2009)
sources.note: Fusing keyword and vector rankings, in reciprocal_rank_fusion.

sources.title: Orca: continuous batching (Yu et al., OSDI 2022)
PagedAttention / vLLM (Kwon et al., 2023)
sources.note: The paged KV cache that sets how many sequences fit on a GPU.

sources.title: SARATHI: chunked prefills (Agrawal et al., 2023)
sources.note: Splitting long prefills so they do not stall decodes.

sources.title: DistServe: disaggregated prefill and decoding (Zhong et al., 2024)
sources.note: Separate GPU pools for prefill and decode, sized to TTFT and TPOT targets.

sources.title: S-LoRA: Serving Thousands of Concurrent LoRA Adapters (Sheng et al., 2023)
sources.note: Batching requests for many adapters over one base model, with an adapter cache.

sources.title: Deep & Cross Network for Ad Click Predictions (Wang et al., 2017)
sources.note: Explicit feature crosses for sparse CTR data.

sources.title: How to Scale Your Model (Google DeepMind)
sources.note: Rooflines and inference arithmetic for transformers, with worked numbers.
